advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the box always has a persistent /var/log/journal (or note that volatile-storage hosts will page both journal alarms), since §2g's du and the ceiling both assume the persistent tree exists.
evidence: render_dropin sets only `SystemMaxUse=${JOURNAL_MAX_USE_BYTES}` under `[Journal]` (journald-cap.sh:112-118); no `Storage=persistent` is written, so persistence of /var/log/journal is assumed, not enforced
ABSENCE: no guard distinguishes "journal is volatile/RAM-only" from "du could not size a persistent journal"; both produce silence and page identically
advisory.finding: observability.sh §2g sizes /var/log/journal with du; on a host running journald in volatile-only mode (Storage=auto with no /var/log/journal directory, e.g. after the dir is removed), du fails and both journal_bytes and journal_used_percent go silent, which under treat_missing_data="breaching" pages both journal alarms even though the journal is healthily in RAM. The drop-in sets only SystemMaxUse and does not pin Storage=persistent, so nothing in this change guarantees the measured tree exists.
scenarios: A host where /var/log/journal is absent or journald falls back to /run/log/journal — both journal alarms page continuously despite no disk problem

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an observability test that leaves JOURNAL_MAX_USE_BYTES unset in the env so the `eval "$(journald-cap.sh --print-env)"` path supplies the cap, asserting journal_used_percent is computed against the cap journald-cap.sh actually renders.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:455-457 comment: 'The ceiling comes from infra/scripts/journald-cap.sh ... so the published "percent of cap" and the cap the box is configured to enforce can never drift apart.'
test_print_env_is_the_single_source_of_truth_observability_reads asserts --print-env OUTPUT only; it does not assert observability.sh consumes that output when the env var is unset.
advisory.finding: The observability.sh drift-prevention contract — that journal_used_percent's denominator is the cap journald-cap.sh renders via `eval "$(bash "$JOURNALD_CAP_SH" --print-env)"` (observability.sh:459, whose comment says 'the published percent-of-cap and the cap the box is configured to enforce can never drift apart') — is never exercised end-to-end: every observability test pre-sets JOURNAL_MAX_USE_BYTES in the process environment, so the `${JOURNAL_MAX_USE_BYTES:-...}` defaulting in journald-cap.sh --print-env is short-circuited and the eval's output is overridden by the injected value. A regression that broke --print-env's emission (or observability's consumption of it) would not fail any test.
scenarios: A refactor of --print-env's variable names or observability.sh's eval that breaks the cap hand-off would leave journal_used_percent measured against a stale/default denominator, undetected by the suite.
